body:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in kv-cache paging on us-west-2

ben-sre: seeing a sudden rise in paging/swap on the gen pool. Started ~4m ago. 60% of nodes have swap > 70%. Latency SLO breaches for /v1/generate routes. Root cause unknown yet.

choi-runtime: pulling logs. We promoted an AWQ/INT8 kernel variant (gptq-awq-int8-v2) to canary traffic last night. If awq path pads KV buffers differently it could blow up memory for long contexts.

eva-ml: confirming traffic shift: ~18% weight to gptq-awq-int8-v2 on chat/content routes. Staging didn't show this because typical sequences were shorter. Production getting some 6k-12k token requests. AWQ pads to 128 bytes blocks in current runtime which increases KV bytes/token.

ben-sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) turn off continuous batching for the affected model variant, 2) reduce max_batch_tokens, 3) force-awq-fallback kernel, 4) bump eviction aggressiveness. Who can make the flag flips?

choi-runtime: I can run those changes. Steps I'll take now:
- disable continuous batching for gptq-awq-int8-v2
  curl -X POST "https://runtime-admin.internal/flags" -d '{"model":"gptq-awq-int8-v2","continuous_batching":false}'

- reduce batching tokens and window:
```
PUT /config/model/gptq-awq-int8-v2
{
  "batching": {"max_batch_tokens":64, "window_ms":8}
}
```

- force kernel fallback to fp16 path on pool=us-west-2
  kubectl -n inference set env ds/runtime KERNEL_OVERRIDE=awq_fp16 --selector=pool=us-west-2

I'll apply in that order and watch paging metrics.

devops-bot: patch started: env update KERNEL_OVERRIDE rolling update -> 22 pods. CI checks OK. ETA ~120s.

ben-sre: 90s after first change: paging rate down ~28%. Swap median down from 72% -> 48%. 95p latency from 1.7s -> 1.05s but SLO still hurt (0.9s target). Two hosts still showing recurring page reclaim loops.

mara-oncall: I'm taking monitoring and customer triage. Tagging @gina-cs and @frank-pm for customer impact comms and PM handoff.

gina-cs: flagged accounts that reported timeouts: acme-corp, delta-ops, edu-labs. Drafting status message: "We're investigating increased latencies related to memory usage; temporarily routing traffic to a fallback model and limiting long-context requests." Will send once we confirm routing change.

choi-runtime: applied eviction tuning for the model cache to be aggressive and shortened TTLs:
```
POST /config/cache/gptq-awq-int8-v2
{
  "eviction_policy":"aggressive",
  "kv_ttl_ms":30000
}
```

ben-sre: after eviction and kernel fallback, paging trending to baseline within 7min. Swap usage under 40% fleet-wide. Latency 95p back to 0.85s. Good but we'll keep mitigations.

eva-ml: running microbenchmarks now to quantify KV bytes/token for awq-int8 vs awq-fallback vs fp16. Early numbers show ~2.6x KV bytes/token for awq-int8 at long seqs due to block alignment.

mara-oncall: we also observed requests bypassing sequence caps: some clients POSTed chunked contexts exceeding 8k tokens. I'm enabling an admission guard to reject >8k tokens temporarily.

choi-runtime: added admission guard: rejects >8192 tokens with 400 + explanatory message. Also set per-model continuous batching to false until we have a fix.

ben-sre: quick telemetry snapshot:
- total requests (10m): 39,120
- requests >4k tokens: ~980
- 95p latency >1s: ~11,300
- server 504s: 0.18% overall
- affected customers >5% errors: acme-corp, delta-ops, edu-labs
No payload truncation; server-side timeouts only.

frank-pm: I'll take handoff in ~8m. Action items for follow-up?

mara-oncall: handoff list for @frank-pm:
- [choi-runtime] attach kernel selection traces and runtime logs to INC ticket (in progress)
- [eva-ml] complete KV-byte microbench and propose kernel/runtime patch (in progress)
- [choi-runtime] keep AWQ variant at 0% routing and don't re-enable continuous batching until validated (done)
- [ben-sre] watch fleet paging for 2h and be ready to throttle hosts or enable memcg caps (ongoing)
- [gina-cs] follow-up customer comms + post-incident note (drafted)
- [mara-oncall] create postmortem and schedule deep-dive tomorrow

choi-runtime: exporting traces and selecting kernel traces now:
curl -X POST "https://observability.internal/export" -d '{"query":"kernel:awq_int8 AND model:gptq-awq-int8-v2","from":"-20m","to":"now"}' > /tmp/awq_kern_traces.json

eva-ml: I'll also run a controlled replay in staging with 10k token sequences and measure eviction rates; will open an MR to clamp AWQ block size or add KV compression if needed.

gina-cs: customer message sent to affected accounts: "We've rerouted traffic to a fallback model and applied temporary limits to very long contexts. Latency is returning to normal. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline to re-enable the optimized kernel."

ben-sre: monitoring: no page faults for 15m, eviction stable. Keeping incident open for postmortem artifacts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated. Ticket: INC-2054209876. Postmortem owner: mara-oncall. Follow-up meeting scheduled: 2054-04-12T14:00Z.

frank-pm: taking overnight watch. Do not reintroduce gptq-awq-int8-v2 until ML/runtime teams provide KV-byte metrics and a regression test for long-contexts. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
